questions.q: According to the lesson, what four things must be pinned together for a training run to be truly reproducible?
options: Only the code and the final model accuracy
Data, code, environment, and parameters
Just the Git commit hash
The cloud provider and the region
questions.explain: Missing any one of data, code, environment, or parameters breaks the reproducibility chain, even if the other three are pinned.

questions.q: Why is a pinned Git commit with an unpinned `requirements.txt` (e.g. `scikit-learn>=1.3`) still a reproducibility risk?
options: Git commits cannot be pinned at all
A new library release matching that open-ended constraint could change a default behavior and silently produce a different model later
requirements.txt files are ignored by Python
This combination is actually fully safe and poses no risk
questions.explain: Pinning code without pinning the exact environment leaves a gap — library updates can change results even when the code itself hasn't changed.

questions.q: What does a `dvc.lock` file record, and why does committing it to Git matter?
options: It records nothing useful and exists only for backward compatibility
It records the exact hash of every pipeline stage's dependencies and outputs, so committing it alongside code lets a later checkout reconstruct the exact data state that ran
It stores the full dataset contents directly inside Git
It only tracks the model's final accuracy metric
questions.explain: Because dvc.lock is a plain, small file, committing it with the code ties a specific code version to a specific data version without bloating the repo.

questions.q: Why does the lesson prefer a container image digest (sha256:...) over a tag like `ml-training:latest` for environment pinning?
options: Digests are easier to type than tags
A tag is mutable and can point to a different image later, while a digest is a content hash that guarantees the exact same image months later
Tags are not supported by Docker
Digests make the container run faster
questions.explain: A mutable tag can silently shift to a new image build; the digest uniquely and permanently identifies the exact image content.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the reproducibility manifest described in the lesson?
options: To replace the need for a model registry entirely
To explicitly link a model version to its git commit, data version, environment digest, and hyperparameters in one file, rather than requiring manual correlation across systems
To store the raw training data permanently
To automatically retrain the model every time it is read
questions.explain: The manifest is a single, explicit record of the full reproducibility chain, making it checkable without reconstructing it by hand from separate systems.
